scores.evidence: Every view opens with a one-line question as its title (e.g. 'A: How does a PR become an advisory Libra check?', 'C: How is a Slack thread reply answered?') plus an audience/scope line ('Engineers onboarding to the Libra product…'). The level of detail (protocols, HMAC, table names) suits onboarding engineers.

Boxes are consistently runtime actors and stores (API process, in-process scheduler, SQLite, ClickHouse, microVM, worker, SaaS). Workflow views zoom in from the overview without mixing in code-level or team boxes. Showing the scheduler as a separate box inside the libra-api container is a legitimate in-process zoom.

The flows are well chosen. Unmet condition: no visible omissions note, so readers can't tell that Libra Issues, PR-maker, Self, billing and the dashboard internals were left out on purpose (that list exists only in the JSON). View 4 also has no link back to the incident_candidates/signal_incidents write, so the 'decide to page' story jumps from evidence reads straight to Slack without showing the decision being persisted.

Most arrows are directed, numbered and labeled with protocol, payload and sync/async. Deductions: (1) In view 1 the async webhook and Events API labels overprint the 'Checks API'/'postMessage' labels and can't be read. (2) View 5 reuses the edge label 'A2/C2 SQL: gate audit, run rows, reply jobs', which is wrong for the Slack flow. (3) View 4 draws the unnumbered AWS/PostHog evidence reads below B5/B6 even though evidence comes before the verdict. View 3 likewise draws 'boot starts job loops' last. Readers can misread the order.

Views 2-6 have labeled containers that separate Exla-run Fly apps (libra-api, worker apps, libra-clickhouse), the customer side, managed SaaS, and the isolated Logs stack. Deductions: the overview (view 1) has no containers, only subtitles. 'Customer AWS' sits inside 'Third-party SaaS (managed)', which blurs a customer-owned account with vendor SaaS. That matters because the trust boundary for AWS is assume-role access to customer resources.

Views 2-6 are clean sequence diagrams: left-to-right lifelines, top-to-bottom order, no crossings. Deductions: in view 1 the edge labels collide into unreadable text, and its labels and the container subtitles in view 3 render at very small sizes on a 1194x834 screen. The note panel takes up the lower third of every view.

Views 2-6 carry a legend: header = boundary, faint guide = actor lifeline, cylinder = store, dashed = async, dotted = local I/O, solid = sync, caller→recipient includes the response. Names are real (otel_spans, sendSlack, /v1/traces). Deduction: the entry view (view 1) has only a prose context line and no line-style legend, and its async edges are illegible, so the first conventions a reader sees are undocumented on screen.

These failure behaviours are visible: B2 'await ack else 503'; notes on 429/503 with Retry-After; HMAC callbacks; read-only sandbox writes; budget-exhaustion fallback to deterministic copy; sendSlack claim gates; delivery_unknown never resent; and the credentialless worker. Missing: the single-process risk (a slow downstream wedges the shared event loop and login breaks, which per-call timeouts guard against), and any visible marking of failure points on the paths themselves rather than in side notes.

Each view shows 'Source review 2026-11-05 · 9f2c0394c · Owner: Viraat · Live runtime NOT verified'. The names match the code (api/src/index.ts mounts /v1 otelRoutes, so /v1/traces is real; the sandbox git-fetches with GITHUB_TOKEN). The score is capped at 3 because the running system wasn't verified, and the Logs ingest path detail is slightly off.

A newcomer can explain the three core flows and the separate Logs product from views 2-6. The overview's garbled labels, the misleading A2/C2 label in the Slack view, and the out-of-order evidence arrows in view 4 would likely need a short verbal correction to avoid misreading.

coldRead: Libra is one Hono/Node process (libra-api on Fly, with a SQLite volume as the source of truth) that everything talks to: the Vercel dashboard, the Claude Code plugin/CLI over MCP, GitHub webhooks and Slack events. Flow A: a GitHub pull_request webhook (HMAC-checked) is gate-audited into SQLite. The API then starts a run-once Fly microVM, which fetches base/head source from GitHub, builds, tests and replays traffic with no LLM, and posts evidence back to an HMAC-protected /internal callback. The API then writes an advisory Check Run plus line comments. Flow B: customer OTEL exporters send spans to /v1/traces. The API waits for ClickHouse to confirm the insert and returns 503 if it doesn't. An in-process priority scheduler reduces spans into incident candidates in SQLite, reads extra evidence from customer AWS and PostHog, asks OpenAI for a Scout verdict, and posts to Slack through sendSlack's evidence and claim gates. Flow C: a signed Slack thread event becomes a durable reply job. Production answers it in-process with the stateless responder (OpenAI Responses API plus tools) and posts one terminal reply. A credentialless Codex worker can do the same by leasing the job, and an ambiguous send is never resent. Separately, Libra Logs is its own card-gated product with its own server and ClickHouse, and it doesn't feed core PR review.
inaccuracies: View 5 (Slack conversation) labels the API→SQLite edge 'A2/C2 SQL: gate audit, run rows, reply jobs'. Gate audits and sandbox run rows belong to the PR flow (api/src/routes/webhooks.ts, api/src/services/pr-sandbox.ts), not to Slack reply-job persistence.

View 6 shows 'Customer OTEL exporters' calling 'HTTPS POST /v1/ingest'. In libra-logs the routes are mounted under /logs/api (libra-logs/apps/server/test/flag.test.ts lists /logs/api/v1/ingest and /logs/api/otlp/v1/logs). Also, /v1/ingest is a JSON endpoint, while OTEL exporters would use the OTLP /otlp/v1/logs path (e2e.test.ts lines 232 and 263).
View 4 groups 'Customer AWS' inside the 'Third-party SaaS (managed)' container. It is a customer-owned account that Libra reads through assume-role credentials, not vendor SaaS.
improvements: Fix the overview (view 1): give the webhook/Events API arrows and the Checks/postMessage arrows separate, non-overlapping paths and labels. Add the line-style legend and Exla-run vs managed containers, so the entry view can be read on its own.

Correct the ordering and labels in the workflow views: in view 4, number the AWS/PostHog evidence reads and draw them before B5/B6, and show the candidate/signal_incidents write that gates the page. In view 5, replace the reused A2/C2 label with a Slack-specific 'C2 SQL: general_question reply job'. In view 3, move the boot edge first.

Put the deliberate omissions (Issues, PR-maker, Self, billing, dashboard internals) and the single-process failure mode (a slow downstream wedges the event loop, guarded by per-call timeouts) in the visible notes, and fix the Logs ingest path to the mounted OTLP/JSON routes.
